ScoreboardCommand/TeamCommand: 26.3 routes the one/many feedback through CommandResponseTracker (counts only nonzero tracks); 26.2 branches manually on names.size() and counts every target. Ported the four divergent paths: (1) set — branch on the target count (a set to 0 with one target is a single success), return value*names.size(); (2) enable — message by names.size(), return the unlocked count, throw enable.failed when none unlocked; (3) team join — count every member, return members.size(); (4) team leave — a teamless member still succeeds and counts, return members.size(). add/remove/reset/display/numberformat/operation were verified equivalent (their Tracker forms already branch on the target count and return the 26.2 totals) and are unchanged. New regression test twenty_six_two_counts_targets_not_successes pins all three divergences; all 9 scoreboard_cmd tests pass.

EffectCommands/EnchantCommand: 26.3 routes the one/many feedback through CommandResponseTracker (counts only successes); 26.2 branches manually on the target count and counts every target. Ported give/clear/enchant: message choice and multiple-count now use the target count; returns stay the success counts; the local Tracker struct is gone. The duration computation was already the 26.2 inline form (instantaneous -> seconds/1, -1 -> -1, else seconds*20, default 600) and is unchanged. The 26.2 getName() (vs 26.3 getDisplayName()) error args are unobservable in the Rust's scope (no team formatting on the handled targets). cargo check clean; no unit tests cover these commands (command_exec harness is the check, blocked by the launch crash).

Sculk: (1) canPlaceGrowth — 26.3 counts the sculk_growth_inhibitors tag (verified present in the 26.3 jar, absent in 26.2); 26.2 counts sculk_sensor/sculk_shrieker blocks explicitly. Both the live (level/sculk.rs) and worldgen (worldgen/sculk.rs) implementations now check the two blocks explicitly; the worldgen inhibitors tag set is gone. (2) ChargeCursor worldgen spread — 26.3 pre-checks 12 blocks (distSq<=144) in getValidMovementPos and kills a stuck cursor; 26.2 checks 15 blocks AFTER the move (closerThan 15.0 of the origin column) and leaves a stuck cursor in place. The worldgen feature now does the post-move 15-block check (dx^2+dz^2>=225) with no stuck-kill; the live cursor already matched 26.2 (no origin check in valid_movement). Sensor/catalyst/shrieker/vein diffs are only setBlockAndUpdate vs setBlock(...,3) plus codecs. sculk tests 3/3 pass.

TestCommand: the entire 26.2-vs-26.3 diff is the cross-dimension re-shape (26.3 looks test blocks up by GlobalPos across dimensions via findSelectedTestPositionsAcrossDimensions; 26.2 uses BlockPos in the source's level only). The Rust is already the 26.2 single-level form (test_runs.rs:212: '26.2 has no dimension on a test'; test_position_in_level; the Finder searches run in the level in place). The 26.3-only finder/display/suggest methods are unported.

ServerClockManager/TimeCommand: 26.3 added five 'already' errors (already_at_time, already_at_time_marker, already_paused, already_running, already_same_rate) and a MoveResult return for moveToTimeMarker; 26.2 has none of them — set/pause/resume/rate/marker-move all act unconditionally (only a missing marker errors, via the boolean moveToTimeMarker). Removed all four already-checks from the /time arms in game/commands.rs. tick(), addTicks, setTotalTicks, setRate, setPaused and wrapTime are identical in both versions modulo the ClockInstance rename; the no-marker error's message-arg order (marker, clock) was already right.

PlayerSocialManager/PresenceHandler/RemoteFriendListUpdateHandler: the diff is the authlib package move (com.mojang.authlib.services.* in 26.3 vs com.mojang.authlib.yggdrasil.* in 26.2) plus 26.3 wrapping the presence post in a try/catch postPresence helper (26.2 calls the service directly). The Rust models the friends service as a local stub with no real network call, so neither difference is observable; the state machine (flags, presence status, update interval) is identical.

NetherFortressPieces/Structure: the piece methods take StructurePiecesBuilder (26.3) vs StructurePieceAccessor (26.2) — a parameter-type rename with identical bodies (verified on NetherBridgePiece.generatePiece and BridgeCrossing); FORTRESS_ENEMIES uses IntProviders in 26.3 vs plain (min,max) ints in 26.2 with the same values (blaze 2-3/10, piglin 4/5, wither skeleton 5/8, skeleton 5/2, magma cube 4/3). The Rust has no FORTRESS_ENEMIES surface.

AdvancementsScreen: tab selection is already the 26.2 left-click form in the Rust (26.3 switched to right-click), the tab icon/title already derive from DisplayInfo (26.2 form; 26.3 takes them as constructor args), AdvancementWidget decompiles identically, and onClose restores the last screen in both versions.
